text: The allotment for the tribe of Judah, clan by clan, reached to the border of Edom, to the Wilderness of Zin in the far south.
Their southern boundary began at the end of the Salt Sea, from the bay that faces south,
ran south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, continued on to Zin, went up south of Kadesh Barnea, passed by Hezron up to Addar, and curved around to Karka.
From there it passed on to Azmon and came out at the Wadi of Egypt, ending at the sea. This shall be your southern boundary.

versions.text: From there it passed on to Azmon and came out at the Wadi of Egypt, ending at the sea. This is your southern boundary.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses the imperfect (יִהְיֶה), a formal declaration of the boundary to the people: "this shall be your southern boundary." The future form also reads with more weight when spoken aloud.

text: The eastern boundary was the Salt Sea as far as the mouth of the Jordan. The northern boundary began at the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Jordan,
went up to Beth Hoglah, passed north of Beth Arabah, and went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
Then it climbed to Debir from the Valley of Achor, turned north to Gilgal, which faces the Ascent of Adummim south of the ravine, and continued on to the waters of En Shemesh, coming out at En Rogel.

From there it ran up the Valley of Ben Hinnom along the southern slope of the Jebusite city—that is, Jerusalem—and on to the top of the hill west of the Hinnom Valley, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim.
From the hilltop the boundary bent toward the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, ran out to the towns of Mount Ephron, and bent toward Baalah, that is, Kiriath Jearim.
Then it curved west from Baalah to Mount Seir, ran along the northern slope of Mount Jearim—that is, Kesalon—went down to Beth Shemesh and crossed to Timnah.
It went on to the northern slope of Ekron, bent toward Shikkeron, passed along to Mount Baalah, and came out at Jabneel, ending at the sea.
The western boundary was the coastline of the Great Sea. These were the boundaries around the people of Judah, clan by clan.
To Caleb son of Jephunneh, Joshua gave a portion among the people of Judah, as the LORD had commanded him: Kiriath Arba, that is, Hebron—Arba being the ancestor of Anak.
Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai, the descendants of Anak.
From there he went up against the inhabitants of Debir, formerly called Kiriath Sepher.
And Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Aksah in marriage to the man who attacks and captures Kiriath Sepher."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, captured it, so Caleb gave him his daughter Aksah in marriage.
When she came to Othniel, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What can I do for you?"
She answered, "Grant me a favor. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well." So he gave her the upper and lower springs.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of Judah, clan by clan.
The southernmost towns of the tribe of Judah, toward the border of Edom in the Negev, were: Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,
Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,
Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan,
Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,
Hazor Hadattah, Kerioth Hezron (that is, Hazor),
Amam, Shema, Moladah,
Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth Pelet,
Hazar Shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah,
Baalah, Iyim, Ezem,
Eltolad, Kesil, Hormah,
Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain and Rimmon—twenty-nine towns in all, with their villages.
In the western foothills: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,
Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, Enam,
Jarmuth, Adullam, Sokoh, Azekah,
Shaaraim, Adithaim and Gederah (or Gederothaim)—fourteen towns with their villages.
Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal Gad,
Dilean, Mizpah, Joktheel,
Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,
Kabbon, Lahmas, Kitlish,
Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah and Makkedah—sixteen towns with their villages.
Libnah, Ether, Ashan,
Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,
Keilah, Akzib and Mareshah—nine towns with their villages.
Ekron, with its surrounding settlements and villages;
from Ekron to the sea, all the territory near Ashdod, with their villages;

versions.text: west of Ekron, all the territory near Ashdod, with its villages;
versions.explanation: וָיָמָּה means "and seaward/to the sea," marking the stretch from Ekron out to the Mediterranean, not merely a location "west of Ekron." Also, וְחַצְרֵיהֶן is plural ("their villages"), matching the plural sense of the territory listed.

text: Ashdod with its surrounding settlements and villages; and Gaza with its settlements and villages, as far as the Wadi of Egypt and the coastline of the Great Sea.
In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Sokoh,
Dannah, Kiriath Sannah (that is, Debir),
Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,
Goshen, Holon and Giloh—eleven towns with their villages.
Arab, Rumah, Eshan,

versions.explanation: The Hebrew text reads רוּמָה (Rumah); "Dumah" reflects an alternate manuscript tradition. Follow the Hebrew and, if desired, add a footnote noting that some manuscripts read "Dumah."

text: Janum, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah,

versions.explanation: The written form is Janim but the read form (qere) is יָנוּם, "Janum," which is the form normally rendered in translation. A footnote could note the alternate spelling "Janim."

text: Humtah, Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron) and Zior—nine towns with their villages.
Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,
Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,
Kain, Gibeah and Timnah—ten towns with their villages.
Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor,
Maarath, Beth Anoth and Eltekon—six towns with their villages.
Kiriath Baal (that is, Kiriath Jearim) and Rabbah—two towns with their villages.
In the wilderness: Beth Arabah, Middin, Sekakah,
Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi—six towns with their villages.

versions.text: Nibshan, the City of Salt and En Gedi—six towns with their villages.
versions.explanation: A comma before "and En Gedi" keeps the list punctuation consistent with verse 61 and marks the pause clearly for a reader speaking the list aloud.

text: The people of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, who were living in Jerusalem; so to this day the Jebusites live there alongside the people of Judah.

versions.text: Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, who were living in Jerusalem; to this day the Jebusites live there alongside the people of Judah.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew subject is "the sons of Judah" (bene Yehudah), and the same phrase is rendered "the people of Judah" later in the verse; matching the two makes the sentence internally consistent for oral reading. Adding "so" reflects the consecutive waw and smooths the transition between the two clauses.
